action.rationale: Budget is only 100 (10×dim) which is below the 20×dim threshold, so run a light probe (P1–P3) to guide method choice without overspending. Evaluations are cheap and deterministic, so a small 12-eval probe balances insight and remaining budget (88).

Budget is small for d=10 (100 total, 88 left) and probes indicate weak global structure (P2 fdc_spearman=0.3706, top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.9165) with no quadratic signal (P3 null). A short race between a model-based method (turbo) and a population method (cma_es) hedges efficiently and should reveal which adapts better within this budget.

With 70 evals left (< 30·dim = 300) and turbo winning the race (best 105.55 vs 117.98) while fresh (evals_in_tenure=0, tr_length=0.8, not exhausted), continuing turbo is sample-efficient. Probes suggest weak global structure (P2 fdc=0.37, top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.92), which favors model-based search like TuRBO.

Only 20 evaluations remain (out of 100), so it’s time to refine the incumbent (99.52 at eval 80). BOBYQA needs 2·dim+1=21 evaluations just to start in 10-D, which exceeds the remaining budget, while L-BFGS-B can take 1–2 steps within 20 evals. TuRBO improved 6.03 over 50 evals but further global search is unlikely to beat a focused polish now.
